text.p: Printed circuit board manufacturer Symonds Plc on Tuesday said pretax profits for the year to March 31, 1997 will be lower than expectations owing to difficult market conditions.
In a trading update, the group said that order shortfalls at two of its divisions lay behind the estimates.

Its finishing services division, which designs and manufactures conveyorised process systems for the printed circuit board industry had experienced a particularly difficult first quarter 1997, after decisions on some major contracts were deferred.
Also, its precision engineering division was hit by the rescheduling of two major contracts in the first quarter, a time traditionally when most of the division's profits are earned.
The annual figures are to be announced on June 19.
Symonds' share price at 1100 GMT was down 21 pence at 38 pence.
